tasks.title: Stand up the sbx runtime package: Backend, Runner seam, Spec, template-ref accessor
tasks.description:
Context
First lap of the sbx-3 batch (CLI runtime backend — the central cutover of the sbx migration). Source: openspec/changes/sbx-3-sbx-runtime-backend/{proposal,design,tasks}.md (tasks 1.1-1.3, 3.1 Spec only, 3.2). sbx-2 has landed: the dune-sbx template (ghcr.io/mitchell-wallace/dune-sbx, version in container/sbx/IMAGE_VERSION) and its login-shell hook that refreshes /workspace from DUNE_WORKSPACE and runs setup-persist once per sandbox. Today's runtime lives in internal/dune/app.go with capture (combined output) and runStreaming (PTY) helpers; internal/version/version.go has BaseImageRef() reading container/base/IMAGE_VERSION.

Outcome
A new internal/dune/runtime/sbx package compiles with: a lifecycle-oriented Backend interface (Validate/Ensure/Start/Shell/Stop/Status) that keeps sbx verbs private to the package (D1); a Runner seam (Capture/Stream) plus a defaultRunner wrapping os/exec that preserves current capture/stream behavior (D5); a fakeRunner test helper recording each invocation (dir, name, args) and returning preset output/errors per call (1.3); and a minimal backend-agnostic Spec carrying only semantic fields — instance name, workspace host path, profile, template ref, working dir, shell, timezone (D2). Plus version.SbxTemplateRef() mirroring BaseImageRef(): an ldflags-injectable repo (ghcr.io/mitchell-wallace/dune-sbx) plus a version that falls back to reading container/sbx/IMAGE_VERSION (NOT top-level VERSION), with a unit test asserting the repo and a non-empty version (D10).

Files & scope
New internal/dune/runtime/sbx/ (backend, runner, spec, fakeRunner in a _test.go); internal/version/version.go (+ its test). Leave app.go untouched this lap. Do NOT remove project{} yet — the still-present Compose path uses it; its removal is the later removal lap.

Design
This is the architectural seam the rest of sbx-3 builds on, so get the boundary right: the interface speaks Dune lifecycle operations, not sbx primitives. Mirror the existing capture/runStreaming semantics in defaultRunner so the later cutover is behavior-preserving. Spec is deliberately minimal (the reshaped successor to ref-1's never-implemented EnvironmentPlan), not generalised for hypothetical backends.

Acceptance
go build ./... and go test ./internal/version/... pass; the new package builds; the SbxTemplateRef() unit test asserts repo + non-empty version. Do not tick any tasks.md boxes (only VERIFY ticks).

tasks.title: Implement sbx readiness validation
tasks.description:
Context
Builds on lap 1's Backend/Runner seam. Tasks 2.1-2.2 and the Validate failure-mode tests in 7.2. This replaces validateDockerPrerequisites (internal/dune/app.go, around line 575). Design D6 pins the exact command shapes.

Outcome
Backend.Validate is implemented against the Runner seam: sbx present on PATH; sbx diagnose --output json reports all checks passing (this also covers daemon health and authentication — the spikes saw 8 checks pass); and the installed sbx version (from sbx version, observed v0.32.0) meets a pinned minimum (candidate v0.32.0). Each unmet requirement returns a clear, actionable error, and no sandbox operation proceeds when validation fails (2.2).

Files & scope
internal/dune/runtime/sbx/ (validation source + tests). Do not wire Validate into app.go yet — that happens in the restructure lap.

Design
The JSON flag is NOT uniform across sbx subcommands: sbx diagnose uses --output json while sbx ls (used later by Status) uses --json (D6). Use diagnose's verified --output json here. Pin the parse shapes in fakeRunner tests so a future sbx flag change surfaces as a failing test. Implement a small semver-style minimum-version comparison rather than a string compare.

Acceptance
go test ./internal/dune/runtime/sbx/... passes, including failure-mode tests (7.2) for: missing sbx (not on PATH), failed diagnose (a check reporting not-passing), and below-minimum version. Tests assert the exact constructed args (sbx diagnose --output json, sbx version). Do not tick any tasks.md boxes.

tasks.title: Build sbx sandbox lifecycle command construction
tasks.description:
Context
The heart of the backend. Tasks 4.1-4.4 plus the command-construction/sequencing tests in 7.1. Depends on laps 1-2. sbx command shapes are confirmed by spike 4 (task 4.0, done): sbx create has no env flag but takes extra positional rw workspaces; sbx exec supports -it/-w/-e and auto-starts a stopped sandbox; start is sbx run <name>; sbx rm needs --force when non-TTY. The dune-sbx template's login hook refreshes /workspace from DUNE_WORKSPACE and runs setup-persist (PERSIST_DIR override, default /persist/agent) once per sandbox, sentinel-guarded.

Outcome
- Ensure (4.1): create the sandbox from the template with the workspace direct-mounted (sbx create --name <instance> --template <ref> shell <absolute host path>), passing the profile-persist host dir as an extra positional rw workspace, then fire the template hook with ONE login exec carrying BOTH env vars — sbx exec -e DUNE_WORKSPACE=<absolute host path> -e PERSIST_DIR=<absolute persist mount path> <instance> bash -lc true (D3/D4).
- Status (4.2) via sbx ls --json (note --json here, not --output json), distinguishing exists-but-stopped from running; Stop via sbx stop <name>; Start via sbx run <instance>.
- Shell (4.3) as sbx exec -it -w <mounted repo path> <instance> zsh, forwarding the caller's TERM/COLORTERM via -e KEY=VALUE (one pair per variable, only when that variable is set) — this carries forward the powerlevel10k 256-colour prompt fix from the Compose attachArgs (app.go around line 600); use the -w fallback shape from design D4 if -w is unsupported.
- Persist mapping (4.4): back /persist/agent with a durable, profile-scoped host dir (e.g. ~/.local/share/dune/persist/<profile>) decoupled from any single sandbox so profile state is shared and survives rebuild (D3). The survival proof is the smoke lap (8.1); here just wire the mount + PERSIST_DIR delivery correctly.
Instance naming is dune-<workspace-slug>-<profile> (D3).

Files & scope
internal/dune/runtime/sbx/ (Ensure/Status/lifecycle/Shell + tests). Still do not gut the Compose path in app.go.

Design
This is the high-risk command-construction core. The persist dir mounts at its ABSOLUTE HOST PATH inside the sandbox (not /persist/agent) — that is exactly why PERSIST_DIR must point setup-persist at the mounted host path. The hook is sentinel-guarded (runs once per sandbox), so PERSIST_DIR must be present on the first, hook-firing exec. Status must read sandbox name + status from sbx ls --json so up reuses a running sandbox without recreation and only Starts when stopped.

Acceptance
fakeRunner command-construction/sequencing tests (7.1) assert the exact sbx args, instance name, mount path, env flags (DUNE_WORKSPACE + PERSIST_DIR on the hook exec; TERM/COLORTERM present-when-set and omitted-when-unset on Shell), and ordering for create/start/attach, running-sandbox reuse, and stop. go test ./internal/dune/runtime/sbx/... passes. go build ./... passes (Compose path still present and intact). Do not tick any tasks.md boxes.

tasks.title: Verify the sbx backend foundations (sbx-3 phases 1-4)
tasks.description:
Context
Mid-change verification after the backend package, readiness validation, and lifecycle command construction are built but before the app.go cutover. Use the openspec-verify-change skill against sbx-3-sbx-runtime-backend, focused on phases 1-4: tasks 1.1-1.3, 2.1-2.2, 3.1 (Spec), 3.2, 4.1-4.4, 7.1, 7.2.

Outcome
A report confirming the Backend/Runner/Spec foundations, Validate, and lifecycle command construction are correct and thorough — not merely that tests are green. Trace the actual constructed sbx argument vectors (create/exec/ls/run/stop). Confirm the hook-firing exec carries BOTH DUNE_WORKSPACE and PERSIST_DIR as the design contract requires; that Shell's TERM/COLORTERM forwarding matches the carried-forward attachArgs behavior (present-when-set, omitted-when-unset); that SbxTemplateRef reads container/sbx/IMAGE_VERSION (not top-level VERSION) with the dune-sbx repo; and that the diagnose/ls JSON flag asymmetry is respected (--output json vs --json).

Design
Identify the intended integration target before diffing — this branch is dunex (the sbx integration line), not main; confirm from repo docs / branch config / recent history rather than assuming, then diff this batch's work against the batch baseline (the sbx-2 close commit). Treat everything before this batch's first lap as pre-existing baseline; do not add cleanup laps for pre-batch work unless the user asks. Do not rewrite git history. You may fix only tiny, safe one-liners; anything larger becomes a new head lap.

Acceptance
Check off tasks.md boxes for phases 1-4 only where verified correct and thorough (1.1-1.3, 2.1-2.2, 3.1, 3.2, 4.1-4.4, 7.1, 7.2). Leave the app.go restructure, removals, smoke, and docs unticked. File any substantive gaps as new head laps.

tasks.title: Close remaining sbx-runtime foundation verification gaps
tasks.description:
Context
VERIFY found two phase-1-4 gaps in sbx-3 before the app.go cutover. First, internal/dune/runtime/sbx/validate.go accepts structurally-empty or drifted sbx diagnose --output json payloads as healthy because it only unmarshals JSON and does not require the expected checks shape, so D6's exact-shape pinning is weaker than intended. Second, task 7.1 is not actually complete yet: the fakeRunner lifecycle suite covers create/start/attach, running reuse, down/stop, and the -w fallback, but it does not cover a rebuild / sbx rm --force sequence.

Outcome
Harden the readiness parser/tests so malformed or shape-drifted diagnose JSON fails validation, and complete or explicitly re-scope the missing rebuild sequencing coverage so task 7.1 only gets ticked when that assertion exists.

Files & scope
internal/dune/runtime/sbx/{validate.go,validate_test.go,lifecycle.go,lifecycle_test.go} and openspec/changes/sbx-3-sbx-runtime-backend/tasks.md if task status changes. Keep the change additive; do not rewrite history.

Acceptance
go test ./internal/dune/runtime/sbx/... passes. Validation rejects missing/shape-drifted diagnose check data. The lifecycle fakeRunner suite either asserts the rebuild / sbx rm --force path explicitly or the task/deferred scope is updated coherently so 7.1 is no longer overstated.

tasks.title: Restructure app.go to resolve-plan-execute and wire commands to the sbx backend
tasks.description:
Context
The central app.go surgery. Tasks 3.3, 5.1-5.4. Depends on the verified backend (laps 1-4). app.go's Run (around line 85) today resolves workspace/profile, builds project{} (around line 69), and drives docker compose for up/down/rebuild/logs.

Outcome
app.go restructured into resolve -> build Spec -> dispatch to the sbx Backend, reusing the existing workspace resolution (git rev-parse --show-toplevel with cwd fallback), the profile store (~/.config/dune/profiles.json), profile-name validation, and timezone logic (3.3). Commands wired (5.1-5.4): up (default) -> Validate -> ensure template available -> Ensure -> Start (if stopped) -> Shell, reusing a running sandbox without recreation (D7); down -> Stop; rebuild -> recreate from the template (sbx rm + Ensure/Start, no Dockerfile.dune build) preserving profile-scoped persisted state via the durable persist location; logs kept functional against the sbx runtime as an interim mapping (finalised in sbx-5); version, profile set, profile list unchanged.

Files & scope
internal/dune/app.go (and the cli option parsing if needed). The Compose helper functions may remain physically present this lap (the next lap removes them) but must no longer be on the active up/down/rebuild/logs path. Build must stay green.

Design
Brownfield architecture work on the production entry point: keep the user-facing command surface and profile semantics intact — only the realisation backend changes. Spec.TemplateRef comes from version.SbxTemplateRef(). Leave the internal/dune/pipelock package present-but-unused — just stop calling ensurePipelockConfig and starting the sidecar on the active path (full package removal is sbx-4, D9). Preserve selfUpdate.

Acceptance
go build ./cmd/dune and go test ./... pass (Compose unit tests may still pass against the now-dormant code until the removal lap). dune up/down/rebuild/logs dispatch through the sbx backend. Do not tick any tasks.md boxes.

tasks.title: Remove the Docker Compose runtime path
tasks.description:
Context
The destructive cutover. Tasks 6.1-6.3, the deferred project{} removal from 3.1, and test retirement 7.3. Depends on lap 5 (app.go already dispatching to the backend).

Outcome
Removed from the active runtime: project{} (D2/D8); the compose template compose.yaml.tmpl; renderComposeFile/ensureComposeFile/validateComposeFile; ensureVolume; prepareAgentImage; composeArgs/composeUp/localImageExists; isAgentRunning/isAgentCreated; validateDockerPrerequisites; the attachArgs/composeShell Compose attach (its TERM/COLORTERM logic now lives in the backend Shell); and Dockerfile.dune detection + the dune-local-<slug>:latest build (UseBuild) (6.1, 6.2). Pipelock startup/wiring removed from the runtime path while leaving the internal/dune/pipelock package present-but-unused — full removal is sbx-4 (6.3). Compose golden/validation/shell-shim tests for the removed path are retired or replaced (7.3). Preserve selfUpdate, the profile store, resolveProfile/validateProfileName, workspace resolution, effectiveTimezone, and the cli option parsing (D8).

Files & scope
internal/dune/app.go, the compose template file, and the associated _test.go files. Do NOT delete the internal/dune/pipelock package (sbx-4 owns that). Do not touch container/base assets.

Design
High-risk brownfield removal. Grep for every reference to each removed symbol before deleting so nothing dangles, and keep each commit building. After removal, confirm via grep that compose, docker compose, Dockerfile.dune, dune-local, and the removed function names have no live references (the dormant pipelock package excepted). Do not rewrite git history — additive/revert commits only.

Acceptance
go build ./cmd/dune and go test ./... pass with the Compose path gone; grep confirms no live references to the removed symbols/templates remain (pipelock package intentionally dormant). Do not tick any tasks.md boxes.

tasks.title: Smoke-verify the sbx runtime against the dune-sbx template
tasks.description:
Context
The empirical gate for the cutover. Tasks 8.1, 8.2. Requires an installed, authenticated sbx (meeting the pinned minimum) and the dune-sbx template (ghcr.io/mitchell-wallace/dune-sbx — pull it, or load locally via docker save + sbx template load per design Open Questions). Per AGENTS.md you may build an ephemeral template image to test against.

Outcome
A smoke test against the installed sbx that: (a) creates a sandbox from the dune-sbx template via Ensure and confirms the attached shell's cwd is the mounted repo path (git rev-parse --show-toplevel succeeds); and (b) gates D3 — writes a sentinel under /persist/agent (into the profile-persist mount), runs sbx rm --force, recreates via Ensure, and confirms the sentinel survives the recreate, proving profile state is decoupled from the sandbox lifecycle. Temporary sandboxes are cleaned up (sbx rm --force) afterward. go build ./cmd/dune and go test ./... pass (8.2).

Files & scope
The smoke test (adjust/add under the existing smoke harness) and internal/dune/runtime/sbx as needed. Remove any temporary sandboxes the test creates.

Design
This is the persistence-survival gate that makes the cutover safe — spike 4 proved the mechanism standalone; this reproduces it through Ensure. The persist mount lands at its absolute host path in the sandbox, so confirm the setup-persist PERSIST_DIR wiring actually resolves the /persist/agent symlinks to the mount. If the smoke reveals a wiring gap, file a focused head lap rather than expanding scope here.

Acceptance
The smoke run demonstrates cwd-at-repo AND sentinel-survives-recreate; build + full test suite green; no leaked sandboxes. Do not tick any tasks.md boxes.

tasks.title: Fix sbx /persist/agent durable mount wiring
tasks.description:
Context
The `dune-a5fa` smoke gate added `test/smoke/sbx-runtime.sh` and ran it against an installed/authenticated `sbx` v0.32.0 plus a locally built/loaded `ghcr.io/mitchell-wallace/dune-sbx:0.4.8` template. The first `dune up` shell proved the attach cwd is the mounted repo path and `/workspace` points at that repo. The D3 persistence half failed: a sentinel written to `/persist/agent/dune-sbx-smoke-sentinel.txt` disappeared after `sbx rm --force` and recreate via `dune up`/`Ensure`.

Diagnosis
`Ensure` currently passes the profile persist host directory as an extra positional workspace and fires the template hook with `PERSIST_DIR=<absolute host persist path>`. That makes home symlinks such as `~/.claude` resolve to the mounted host path, but `/persist/agent` itself remains the sandbox-local image directory. Therefore writes made directly under `/persist/agent` do not land in the durable profile persist mount and are lost on sandbox removal.

Outcome
Adjust the sbx runtime/template wiring so `/persist/agent` itself resolves to the durable profile-scoped mount while preserving the existing `DUNE_WORKSPACE` `/workspace` contract and the setup-persist first-login behavior. Keep the command construction pinned with fakeRunner tests. Re-run `test/smoke/sbx-runtime.sh` against the loaded or rebuilt `dune-sbx` template; it must demonstrate both cwd-at-repo and `/persist/agent` sentinel survival across `sbx rm --force` + `Ensure` recreate.

Acceptance
`test/smoke/sbx-runtime.sh` passes; `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./...` pass; no temporary sandboxes are leaked (`sbx ls --json` has no smoke sandbox). Do not tick OpenSpec `tasks.md` boxes.

tasks.title: Document the sbx runtime cutover
tasks.description:
Context
Task 8.3. The backend, cutover, removals, and smoke verification are done.

Outcome
Architecture/README docs updated to state: sbx (installed, authenticated, daemon healthy, minimum version) replaces Docker as the host prerequisite; the runtime launches the dune-sbx template instead of a Compose pair; Dockerfile.dune and the compose path are gone; and a note on the one-time transition from Docker Compose workspaces (existing Compose containers/volumes are not auto-migrated — full cleanup is sbx-6).

Files & scope
README / architecture docs, and the AGENTS.md 'Architecture: host vs container' section if it now misdescribes the runtime. Do NOT change the version-bump checklist lockstep target — that is sbx-6's job.

Design
Descriptive, not a redesign. Match the surrounding docs' tone and depth. The AGENTS.md dunex-branch section already documents the migration strategy; only adjust it where it now reads as stale post-cutover.

Acceptance
Docs describe the sbx runtime accurately, with no references implying Docker Compose is still the active backend except clearly-labelled migration/cleanup notes. Do not tick any tasks.md boxes.

tasks.title: Final sbx-3 acceptance: verify the cutover and close the change
tasks.description:
Context
Final full-change verification of the central cutover. Use the openspec-verify-change skill against sbx-3-sbx-runtime-backend across all phases, and inspect the whole diff for the change.

Outcome
A report confirming the full outcome: Docker is no longer a host prerequisite; app.go dispatches to the sbx Backend via resolve -> build Spec -> execute; the Compose path, Dockerfile.dune build, and Pipelock startup are gone from the active runtime (the pipelock package intentionally remains dormant for sbx-4); the smoke gate (cwd-at-repo + persist-survival) was actually demonstrated, not just asserted; and docs are updated. Trace the real cutover — the constructed sbx arg vectors, the symbols actually removed (grep clean), and the TERM/COLORTERM carry-forward in Shell — not just green tests.

Design
Identify the intended integration target before diffing (this branch is dunex, the sbx integration line, not main — confirm from repo docs / branch config / history). Identify this batch's first lap and treat earlier branch work (through the sbx-2 close) as pre-existing baseline; do not remove pre-batch work unless the user asks. Do not rewrite git history; if scope cleanup is needed, add a focused additive/revert lap or ask the user. Confirm the sbx-4 boundary is respected: the pipelock package is still present-but-unused and the docs note the interim egress window.

Acceptance
Run go build ./cmd/dune + go test ./... and the smoke verification; review the whole diff against the integration target; then check off all remaining tasks.md boxes verified correct and thorough (3.3, 5.1-5.4, 6.1-6.3, 7.3, 8.1-8.3, plus any phase-1-4 boxes not already ticked). File substantive gaps as new head laps rather than fixing in place beyond tiny one-liners.
